main_body: Dark stone pillar shaft with three gold rune rings, between a lighter grey cap block at the top and a matching base block at the bottom
top_band: Light grey (#73717c, L=115) at rows 9-11, then a 1-row highlight (#8a8894, L=138) at row 12, then a darker lip (#45434c, L=69) at rows 13-14. The cap is only slightly lighter than its own highlight, so the top face is about 3 rows.
evidence: The cap is a wider plate with rounded corners, but its light rows are only 3 (rows 9-11, L=115). Row 12 is a 1-row edge highlight and rows 13-14 are the darker lip, so these are not top-face rows. The cap reads as a front-view bevelled block, not an elliptical top seen from above. Rule 12 needs at least 4 clearly lighter top-face rows, so it fails. The shaft is a flat dark vertical face (L=37-69) with painted gold rings and no inset. The bottom block repeats the same front-on construction.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral (#19171c), so the outline is a near-black sticker line, unlike the tinted outlines of the references. The caps have a few grey steps, but the shaft is a near-uniform dark fill with no grain or per-stone shading. The 5x5 flat-fill measure is 0% only because the piece is narrow. It is clearly thinner and flatter than the Beodeul props.
